__doc: Attributes that MUST carry block_attributes.role = 'scalar-media'. THE source of truth for that assignment. db_lookup._migrate_scalar_media_roles() re-applies it at module load.
__why: This is a RE-BUILD of a mechanism that was lost, not a new feature. D128 (2026-06-01) built art-directed media routing and set this role with a HAND-TYPED DB UPDATE that was never captured in any migration, seed or script — it was recorded only as a note marked 'DB (gitignored)'. Nothing could reproduce it, so it silently reverted, and the auto-classifier refilled the blank with its generic name-regex guess 'image-object'. Measured 2026-08-02: 0 rows carried the role, and a hero clone put the MOBILE image into the DESKTOP attribute while dropping the desktop image into a stray child block. A real clone (sandybrown post 65, backed up 2026-07-16) proves it once worked: splitImage=IMG_20260419_173547_107-7.webp, splitImageMobile=aesthetic-pic-7.jpeg.
__what_the_role_does: Two things, and only the FIRST was superseded. (1) It removes the attr from the universal walk's candidate set, because 'scalar-media' is not in _content_bearing_roles() — so leg 2 stops claiming the image. FR-31-2.6's emit_shape='nested' now also achieves 'no child block', which is why this half looked redundant. (2) It opens run_mechanism_b branch A, the ONLY code path that reads each image's BEM --mobile/--desktop modifier and routes to base vs base+'Mobile'. NOTHING replaced (2). Do not conclude this role is redundant because emit_shape exists — that reasoning was made and measured false on 2026-08-02.
__why_not_modifier_aware_resolution: The alternative considered was making element resolution modifier-aware instead. It does NOT work on the real markup: the live mockup emits TWO classes on each image ('sgs-hero__split-image sgs-hero__split-image--mobile'), and _family_element() returns on the FIRST parseable class, which carries no modifier. Branch A already scans every class for a modifier, which is exactly what the real markup needs. Also, --mobile/--desktop are a minority of modifiers in the corpus (--trial is the most common at 16 instances) and a full-token-first strategy is safe against those only by accident, not by design.
__proven: Sandbox experiment 2026-08-02 against a COPY of the live DB, real two-class markup, real run_universal_content_walk: BEFORE splitImage=/hero-mob.jpg + stray ChildBlock; AFTER applying these 3 rows splitImage=/hero-desk.webp, splitImageMobile=/hero-mob.jpg, no stray child.
__format: [block_slug, attr_name, note] — the role applied is always 'scalar-media'
__roster_source: D128's stated roster, re-verified against the live DB 2026-08-02: all three currently hold role='image-object' with canonical_slot='media'.
attrs: Desktop half of the hero split art-direction pair. Branch A routes the un-suffixed image here.
Mobile half. Branch A routes the --mobile image here by appending 'Mobile' to the base attr name.
__WHY_TESTIMONIAL_SLIDER_IS_EXCLUDED: ⛔ sgs/testimonial-slider.sideImage was briefly added to this roster on 2026-08-02 and it BROKE THE BLOCK. Measured with the seeder disabled: role='image-object' lifts sideImage correctly; role='scalar-media' lifts NOTHING. Reason: scalar-media is not a content-bearing role, so it removes the attr from the universal walk's candidate set — and the path that is supposed to take over, run_mechanism_b branch A, only fires for is_class_section_block blocks. sgs/testimonial-slider returns False, so the attr ends up with no route in either direction. D128's own note said exactly this ('testimonial-slider.sideImage NOT routed — tier=block not class-section, gate doesn't fire; DB row not updated') and deliberately left it alone; adding it here overrode a documented decision with an assumption. ⚠ PRE-CONDITION for ever adding a block to this roster: db_lookup.is_class_section_block(slug) MUST return True. scalar-media only pays off when branch A can actually fire; on any other block it strands the attr with no route at all.
